description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of attribution evaluation across various domains in the context of large language models, as presented in the paper “Automatic Evaluation of Attribution by Large Language Models.” The chart is divided into 12 distinct categories, each represented by a uniquely colored wedge with corresponding percentage labels and leader lines. The largest segment, colored bright blue, represents “AI/NLP Research” at 24.3%, followed by “Econ. & Fin.” in teal at 18.4%. Other notable segments include “History” and “Game&Anime,” both at 8.2%; “Daily Life” at 7.1%; “Med & Health” and “Science,” both at 6.7%; “Pet & Animal” at 5.5%; “Law” at 5.1%; “Business” at 5.9%; “Geography” at 2.7%; and “Math” at 1.2%. The chart uses a clear legend-style labeling system with lines pointing to each wedge, and the segments are arranged in a roughly descending order clockwise from the top right, though not strictly sorted. No slices are exploded or emphasized visually beyond their proportional size and color differentiation.
